en_alt: The child was frightened of the big pig.
The child got scared of the big pig.
note: "was frightened of" is the more usual English for испугаться + genitive; en_gb still reads fine.

ru: В шкафу́ лежи́т мно́го тёплых сви́теров.
en_alt: There are a lot of warm jumpers in the wardrobe.
There are many warm jumpers in the cupboard.
note: "lie in the wardrobe" is the literal reading; the existential version is what an English speaker would say.

en_alt: The criminal is still free.
The criminal is still at liberty.
note: "at large" is the right idiom but hides на свободе; a literal alternative helps the word-bank drill.

en_alt: The bird lived free.
The bird lived in the wild.
note: на свободе of an animal is normally "in the wild"; en_gb stays literal.

en_alt: Scientists are studying the properties of the metal.
note: Imperfective present also reads naturally as the continuous in English.

en_alt: This material possesses a useful property.
note: обладать is "possess"; the literal alternative teaches the instrumental government.

en_alt: There is no mobile signal in the mountains.
note: "signal" is the everyday English here; en_gb keeps the headword gloss.

ru: Э́та це́рковь названа́ в честь свято́го.
en_alt: This church is named in honour of a saint.
note: The literal alternative teaches the phrase в честь.

en_alt: Icons depict saints.
note: The impersonal plural also maps onto an active English sentence.

en_alt: Take the change, please.
note: The Russian has no possessive; "the change" is the literal reading.

en_alt: I won't give away your secret.

ru: Из ма́ленького се́мени вы́росло большо́е де́рево.
en: A big tree grew from a small seed.
en_alt: A big tree grew out of a small seed.
note: ма́ленький is "small"; "tiny" states a degree the Russian does not.

ru: Весно́й мы се́яли семена́ в саду́.

en_alt: There is a lot of fresh hay in the shed.
note: сара́й is glossed "shed"; both renderings are fine.

en_alt: The horse was fed hay.
They fed the horse hay.
note: Impersonal plural; the active version is equally valid English.

en_alt: The heart is beating fast.
The heart beats quickly.
The doctor is listening to the heart.
The doctor listens to how the heart is working.
note: "the work of the heart" is close to translationese; en_gb kept because it preserves рабо́ту, alternatives added.

en_alt: By the middle of the day it became hot.
We reached the middle of the journey.
We got halfway along the way.
note: "the middle of the way" is marginal English; "journey" is the natural rendering of путь here.

en_alt: Two sergeants were standing on the parade ground.
The sergeant trained the recruits.
The soldiers were listening to the sergeant.

ru: В де́тстве я де́лала уро́ки вме́сте со сёстрами.
en_alt: As a child I did homework together with my sisters.

en: My sister likes the new job.
en_alt: My sister likes her new job.
The new job appeals to my sister.
note: The Russian says only "the new job"; "her" invents the possessor.

en_alt: He bought presents for the sisters.
He bought his sisters presents.
note: The Russian has no possessive; the alternative keeps the drill from rejecting it.

en_alt: My sister is older than I am.
I gave a book to my sister.
I gave my sister a book as a present.
note: подари́ть is specifically to give as a gift.
The English "net" is right for сетка in a sports sense, but the headword gloss is only "grid" — the gloss is likely the half that needs widening to "grid/net/mesh".

en_alt: The window is covered with a fine mesh.
The window is covered by a fine net.
note: Same gloss tension as the sibling sentence; the translation itself is right.

en_alt: Draw the table in the form of a grid.
note: The literal alternative teaches в ви́де.

ru: Магази́н име́ет се́ти по всей стране́.
note: A single магази́н "having networks" is not idiomatic Russian — the natural phrasing is сеть магази́нов (a chain of shops) or У магази́на есть сеть по всей стране́; flagged rather than rewritten because the plural се́ти may be the drilled form.

en_alt: The phone did not find a network.
note: The Russian has no modal; the literal alternative is worth accepting.

en_alt: Siberia is famous for its thick forests.
He quit smoking cigarettes.
He stopped smoking cigarettes.
There was one cigarette left in the packet.
He finds the smell of the cigarette unpleasant.
note: en_gb is literal and defensible; the alternative is the more idiomatic English.

en_alt: Everyone stood up at the signal.
On the signal everyone stood up.

ru: Кора́бль отвеча́л на сигна́лы с бе́рега.
en_alt: The ship was answering signals from the shore.
The ship replied to signals from the shore.
A child was sleeping on the back seat.
note: спал is imperfective; the continuous is the more natural English here.

ru: Он за́нял свобо́дное сиде́нье в авто́бусе.
en_alt: He took a free seat on the bus.
note: "on the bus" is the usual English preposition.

en_alt: After the illness he was gathering his strength.
The artist drew a peace symbol.

ru: В э́том си́мволе есть глубо́кий смысл.
en_alt: There is a deep meaning in this symbol.
note: Uncontracted form so the word-bank drill accepts it.

en_alt: The patient developed a new symptom.

ru: Они́ пошли́ в синаго́гу в суббо́ту.
В це́нтре го́рода стои́т ста́рая синаго́га.
en_alt: An old synagogue stands in the centre of the city.
We hung up feed for the tits.
note: корм is glossed "feed"; both readings are natural.

en_alt: In winter the tit flies to the window.
The school has a new system of marks.
There is a new system of marks at the school.
note: оце́нка is glossed "mark"; the literal alternative keeps that link.

ru: Он легко́ выхо́дит из ра́зных ситуа́ций.
en_alt: He easily gets out of different situations.
We ended up in a difficult situation.
This is a very complicated situation.
note: сло́жный is glossed "complex"; "complicated" keeps that link.

en_alt: This fairy tale has a good ending.
note: до́брый is "kind/good"; "happy ending" is the idiomatic English, the literal alternative keeps the gloss visible.

en_alt: Grandmother is reading a fairy tale to the grandchildren.

ru: В газе́тах писа́ли о большо́м сканда́ле.
en_alt: The newspapers were writing about a big scandal.
After that there were a lot of scandals.
Because of the scandal the minister resigned.
note: ушёл here reads as resigning; en_gb keeps the literal "left".

en_alt: A stain remained on the tablecloth.
A spot was left on the tablecloth.
They laid a white tablecloth on the table.
note: Impersonal plural; the active version is equally valid.

en_alt: There are a lot of bones in a person's skeleton.

ru: На уро́ке мы изуча́ли скеле́т челове́ка.
en_alt: In the lesson we were studying the human skeleton.
During the sale season there are a lot of discounts.
There is a big discount on these goods.
note: това́р is glossed "goods"; the alternative keeps that link.

en_alt: The shop gives students a discount.
The van brought the boxes to the warehouse.
The truck brought the boxes to the warehouse.
note: маши́на is glossed "car"; "lorry" is a reasonable contextual read, so alternatives rather than a rewrite.

en_alt: New warehouses were built in the city.
They built new warehouses in the city.
note: го́род is glossed "city"; the alternative keeps that link.

en_alt: The goods are kept in the warehouse.
The children were sledging down the slope.
A forest grows on the mountain slope.

en: The train goes at great speed.
en_alt: The train is travelling at great speed.
The train goes at high speed.
note: "at a great speed" with the article is not idiomatic English; the bare noun phrase is.

en_alt: The car reduced speed.
The car slowed down.
I have run out of sellotape.
My sticky tape has run out.
She is learning to play the violin.
There are a lot of violins in the orchestra.

ru: Мы умира́ли со ску́ки на уро́ке.

en_alt: Out of boredom I began to read.
Sweet things are her main weakness.
After the illness he feels weak.
note: "feels weakness" is the literal reading; "feels weak" is what an English speaker would say.

en_alt: Fame came to him late.
note: сла́ва here is closer to "fame" than "glory"; the headword gloss may be worth widening.

en_alt: He dreams about glory.
He dreams of fame.
The soldiers were fighting for the sake of glory.
note: ра́ди is "for the sake of"; the literal alternative teaches it.

en_alt: The dog is going along the trail.
The dog is following the trace.
note: идти́ по следу́ is idiomatic "follow the trail"; the literal alternative keeps the headword gloss visible.

en_alt: Birds' tracks are visible on the ground.
Traces of birds are visible on the ground.

en: A trace was left in the snow.
en_alt: A track was left in the snow.
A footprint was left in the snow.
note: English says a mark is left "in" the snow, not "on" it.

en_alt: The case was passed to another investigator.
They handed the case to another investigator.

note: Here сле́дствие means "consequence", a sense the headword gloss "investigation" does not cover — the English is right, so the gloss is probably the half to widen.

en_alt: The investigation continued for several months.
The investigation lasted several months.
The police started an investigation.
She wiped her tears.
She wiped the tears away.
There are a lot of dictionaries in the library.
Look up this word in the dictionary.
According to the neighbour, the house is being sold.
It is difficult to express this in words.

ru: Свою́ мысль он вы́разил просты́ми слова́ми.
en: He expressed his thought in simple words.
en_alt: He put his thought into simple words.
note: вы́разить is "express"; the literal rendering is perfectly natural English here.

en_alt: Write these words down in the notebook.
note: The Russian has no possessive; the alternative is the literal reading.

en_alt: I do not know this word.
The earth is covered with a layer of snow.
note: Земля́ is glossed "earth"; the alternative keeps that link.

en_alt: A layer of dust lies on the table.
